sections.title: Lesson 8.1: Calculating Yields and Returns
sections.overview: This lesson covers the core return calculations tested on the SIE: current yield (also called dividend yield for stocks), capital gains and losses from closing positions, and total return, which combines income with realized or unrealized gains/losses. All yields and returns are expressed on an annualized basis as a percentage of cost or market value.
key_concepts: Current Yield (CY) measures annual income as a percentage of current market price; applies to both stocks and bonds.
When a stock pays a dividend on a quarterly basis, the quarterly dividend must be multiplied by 4 to annualize before computing CY.
For preferred stock, the stated dividend rate is applied to par value ($100 unless stated otherwise) to derive the annual dividend.
Open position = security still held; closed position = security sold (or bought back, in a short sale).
Capital gain/loss is realized only when a position is closed.
Adjusted cost basis reflects modifications from corporate actions such as stock splits or stock dividends.
Total return blends income (dividends/interest) with capital appreciation or depreciation, expressed as a % of cost basis.
Total return may use realized gains/losses (closed positions) or unrealized gains/losses (open positions).
Unrealized gains and losses have no immediate tax impact.
rules: No specific FINRA/SEC rule citations for yield mechanics; calculations follow standard industry conventions.
Cost basis adjustments following stock splits and stock dividends are required for accurate gain/loss calculation.
formulas: Current Yield (CY) = annual income (in dollars) / current market value
Dividend Yield (preferred) = (rate × par) / current market price
Capital Gain or Loss = sales proceeds − adjusted cost basis  (positive = gain; negative = loss)
Total Return = (income + capital gains − capital losses) / cost basis
Adjusted Cost Basis after split = original cost basis / split ratio
mnemonics: "AIM" for Current Yield: Annual Income ÷ Market price.
"PIG" for Total Return: Proceeds-gain + Income, all over cost basis (Gain + Income).

sections.title: Lesson 8.2: Taxation
sections.overview: This lesson distinguishes the categories of taxable income (earned, investment/portfolio, passive) and explains the treatment of capital gains and losses. It also covers holding-period rules for long- vs. short-term classification, the use of losses to offset gains and ordinary income, carryforward rules, and the wash sale rule.
key_concepts: Ordinary income = earned income + investment (portfolio) income + passive income + short-term capital gains.
Earned income: salary, wages, bonuses, tips, self-employment income; only earned income qualifies for IRA contributions.
Investment/portfolio income: dividends and interest.
Passive income: derived primarily from DPPs/limited partnerships and many real estate investments.
Passive losses may offset ONLY passive income—not earned or portfolio income.
Short-term capital gain: position held one year or less; taxed as ordinary income.
Long-term capital gain: position held MORE than one year; taxed at favorable (lower) rate.
Capital losses offset capital gains dollar-for-dollar.
Net capital losses may offset up to $3,000 of ordinary income per year.
Excess losses are carried forward indefinitely (no time limit) until used up.
Unrealized gains/losses (open positions) have NO tax impact.
Wash sale rule: a loss is disallowed if the same or substantially identical security is repurchased within 30 days before or after the sale establishing the loss (61-day window total).
Wash sale rule applies to recreating long positions AND short positions.
Substantially identical securities include call options, rights, warrants, and convertible bonds/preferred stock of the same issuer that can be converted/exercised into the security sold.
A wash sale is not illegal; only claiming the disallowed loss for tax purposes is illegal.
rules: IRC wash sale rule: 30 days before and 30 days after the sale (61-day window); disallowed loss is added to basis of replacement security.
$3,000 annual limit on net capital losses applied against ordinary income.
IRA contribution eligibility based on earned income only.
formulas: Net Capital Gain/Loss = total capital gains − total capital losses
If Net Loss: Ordinary income reduction = lesser of (net loss) or $3,000; remainder carried forward
Holding period test: > 1 year = long term; ≤ 1 year = short term
Wash sale window = sale date ± 30 days (61 days total including sale date)
mnemonics: "EIP" components of ordinary income: Earned, Investment, Passive.
"30/30" wash sale: 30 days before, 30 days after.
"3K Rule": $3,000 max ordinary income offset per year.
